title: lightweight-rollout-patterns-scratchpad
content:
Goal: sketch a small-footprint rollout pattern that lets product teams ship latency-sensitive LLM features with minimal infra/ops touch. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, lots of TODOs.

Problem statement
- Teams want to try model upgrades (new weights or quant profiles) or enable expensive features (function-calling, longer context) behind gradual exposure but don’t want full dedicated capacity.
- Current canary+dedicated flows are heavy: infra tickets, capacity budgeting, long lead times.
- Hosted API customers need a fast, low-friction way to gate features and roll back if cost/latency/regressions occur.

Design goals (non exhaustive)
1) Low operational overhead for product teams (self-serve).
2) Strong safety: fast rollback, deterministic fallback rules.
3) Cost-aware defaults so experiments don’t blow credits.
4) Telemetry hooks for signal (latency, per-token cost, hallucination rate on eval set).
5) Work for Hosted/Dedicated/Private with minimal differences.

Core idea: "lightweight rollouts" = a routing layer + policy DSL that lives in console + small API flags. No extra GPU pool required for 0→X% traffic; use multiplexing and on-demand routing to model variant when capacity allows else fallback.

Scheme sketches
A) Percent-based sampling with soft cap
- User sets two model variants: base and candidate.
- Target exposure: 0–X% of requests (traffic sampled by user id/region/route).
- Soft cap: if candidate exceeds per-second token budget (configurable), sampling automatically throttles back to keep cost.
- Fallback behavior: when candidate not available (capacity or cost), route to base.

B) Route-by-latency budget
- Each API route gets an SLO target (p95 latency).
- Requests assigned to candidate only if estimated added latency < budget margin (cheap heuristic using token length estimate + known model delta).
- Useful for features that are only occasionally heavy.

C) Feature-flag style: "managed bursts"
- Allow short bursts (N requests per minute) directed to candidate for focused tests (e.g., A/B experiments with human raters).
- Burst quota consumed and visible in console.

API surface (rough)
- POST /rollouts -> create rollout with fields: name, base_model, candidate_model, selector (percent|user-seg|latency-budget), max_token_budget_per_minute, start_time, end_time, monitoring_hooks (eval_prompt_set id).
- PATCH /rollouts/{id}/pause, /resume, /scale.
- Response headers: X-Rollout-Id, X-Rollout-Path (for tracing).

Console UX notes
- Quick-create modal: pick route, pick candidate, choose selector. Show estimated cost delta and latency delta (from catalog).
- Timeline visualization: projected exposure vs budget, current token burn, recent regressions (if eval set enabled).
- One-click rollback -> immediately sets candidate exposure to 0 and drains in-flight gracefully.

Telemetry & quality signals
- Always capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token cost, candidate vs base output quality (user supplied eval prompts + automatic similarity checks), error rate, cache hit rate (if prefix caching used).
- Lean alerting: a single configable threshold for automated pause (eg: cost > 2x expected OR p95 > baseline + 400ms OR quality drop > X%).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Create + enable a percent rollout against hosted routes via Console + API.
- Live dashboard showing exposure, token burn, latency delta.
- Automatic fallback to base if candidate unavailable.
- Able to pause/resume via API.

Edge considerations
- Stateful features: chat with long KV caches — when sampling between models with incompatible KV formats, we must route consistently by session id to avoid corruption. Add selector options: per-session sticky routing.
- Cache warming: candidate cold start latency. Consider a pre-warm option (small reserved burst capacity) for short bursts.
- Billing visibility: show estimated incremental cost vs baseline in console; warn if over free credits.

Open questions / TODOs
- Selector DSL semantics: how expressive do we want? percent + sticky-by-session + user-seg + latency-budget seems enough for MVP.
- How to estimate candidate latency in polyglot infra? Need model profiler data + historical distributions. Work with runtime/observability to get an API.
- Policy for Private deployments: should rollouts be purely local? Is centralized control plane required? (ask SPM: @Priya)
- Safety net: who can set auto-pause thresholds? product owners only? infra/admins?
- Billing model for Dedicated customers — do we charge for candidate traffic as normal? Need finance input.

Notes to self
- Check with Ethan about adding a small sampling flag to SDK (python/js) so client-side feature flags can co-locate with rollout ID.
- Prototype the console mockup in Figma quick frame.
- Wire up an internal eval prompt set to test hallucination/regression detection; maybe reuse existing hosted-api/evals repo.

Risks
- Overcomplexity: building a general DSL invites scope creep. Keep MVP minimal.
- Incorrect exposure estimates could burn customer credits / cause latency regressions. Need throttle safety defaults.

Next steps (week 1)
- Sync with runtime (Ethan) and observability (Amina) to confirm available signals and APIs. (meeting: Weds)
- Draft API proto + example payloads (this doc -> API PR).
- Console: create two mock screens (create modal + timeline) and get quick feedback from two PMs.
- Create JIRA epic and link here.

References and inspiration
- Existing canary practice notes (internal confluence)
- Feature-flag systems (split, launchdarkly ideas)
- Prior experiment: "dedicated-mini-canary" (notes in ENG-1922)

Final messy checklist
- [ ] Confirm token budget API from runtime
- [ ] Add sample SDK header to repo
- [ ] Mock console screens
- [ ] Write acceptance test (simulate candidate outage -> fallback)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and invite stakeholders

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally rough. Keep light and iterate.
